_comment: In-app events. These appear on the product page, in search results and in the Today/Arcade-adjacent surfaces, and they give a reason to open the app that a static listing cannot. Read by node scripts/asc/grow.mjs events. Every event must be true: an event that promises a sale that does not exist gets rejected in review and, worse, teaches users to ignore the next one.
_purchaseComment: No event here is gated on a subscription, so the badge does not imply a purchase. An event that quietly requires Pro is a review rejection and a bait-and-switch.
_territoriesComment: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3, the format appEvent.territorySchedules expects. This is the same 40 markets the tier-1 and tier-2 listing effort targets, not a guess at 'everywhere': an event with no localized copy running in a storefront we cannot write for is noise.
_limitsComment: Apple's documented characters-per-field and window limits. They are enforced client-side by grow.mjs so an over-long localized description fails before an API call, not as a 409 that names no field. The server is the real authority; if a value passes here and Apple rejects it, grow.mjs prints Apple's own detail text.
_localeComment: Locales with hand-written copy. An event with English text in a Japanese storefront is worse than no event there.
